fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 does not specify how an arbitrary BMT moving span embeds into a fixed polynomial-size AG evaluation family; generic generator columns do not lie on an RS/AG evaluation variety. Low Schur dimension over an extension field also gives neither binary Hamming support nor the required all-mixed-word distance, and the proposed search has no frozen family or acceptance threshold.

Proposal 2 cannot seal the known affine-closure attacks while every proper matching activates zero collision features. Any odd linear combination of legal lifted matchings also has zero in every such tree or collision-monomial coordinate, including a complete algebra on a bounded component; logarithmic depth additionally lacks the required bounded-degree and polynomial-output reduction.

Proposal 3 is only a linear rank/nonvanishing condenser. Hasse derivatives can show that a polynomial survives somewhere but do not force large binary support or control worst-case YES density; inherited linear cube relations remain, and exponents, evaluation points, derivative multiplicities, and the exact binary map are not fully frozen.

Proposal 4 constructs labels from an enumeration of dangerous low-weight words or circuits, which becomes the hard decoding task when the protected threshold grows. Constant-weight enumeration cannot prove a polynomial gap, while a positive tiny SAT solution would not establish polynomial-time constructibility or protect unlisted mixed words; the label rule and position separation are also unspecified.

Proposal 5 has no polynomial binary linearization. Fixed-degree Magnus/Fox truncation is a bounded-degree fingerprint vulnerable to larger cube relations, while exact words have exponential dimension; representing nonlinear cover fingerprints requires exponential cover columns or circuit/tableau compilation that re-enters O2/O5.

Proposal 6 is nonlinear in the selected fiber word: x mapped to its locator polynomial is not a linear column operation. Explicit locator generators enumerate an NP-hard fiber, whereas multiplication circuits re-enter the established tableau/exact-fiber obstructions; the tiny row-reduction test cannot address this construction barrier.

Proposal 7 supplies no explicit Puiseux representation, retained minor family, valuation-to-binary metric, fixed target, or rank bound. All compounds are exponential, while greedily selecting minors after enumerating hostile covers is post-hoc and can hide the source decision; sampled minors have no theorem against arbitrary superpositions.

Across all proposals, no candidate supplies an explicit polynomial-time H and t, a universal YES-cost bound, polynomial rank and bit complexity, and a NO invariant covering every mixed word. Therefore none meets the minimum pre-implementation specification, and none offers a genuinely discriminating bounded experiment.
evidence: The collision-walk verifier found finite amplification on selected instances but explicit all-eight and twisted-holonomy illegal mixed words of costs 6 and 9 whose entire feature shell cancels. This directly defeats Proposal 2's claimed sealing mechanism.

The frozen F8 condenser had no pointed kernels yet produced worst YES 31 versus best NO 6. This is exact evidence that rank or polynomial nonvanishing, including the mechanism proposed in Proposal 3, does not imply Hamming support separation.

Code-dependent generator-type puncturing, modular folds, sparse hashes, noncommutative multiplication, and polar shortening all lost the finite gap. Exact parity-check simplification is rigorously vacuous on BMT reduced tensors because their relevant kernels have distance at least three.

Complete product-function compression has the proved rank lower bound sum over j at most r of binomial(k,j), reaching 2^k-1. This blocks Proposal 1 unless its unprovided AG embedding proves a fundamentally different sparse mixed-word representation.

The exchange-quotient verifier found 32 instances where illegal covers lie in the affine span of legal matchings. Any proposed feature shell that vanishes uniformly on legal lifts must explicitly defeat this affine closure rather than merely detect local collisions or holonomy.
No supplied verifier implements any of these seven proposals, so their expected experimental outcomes are unsupported predictions rather than evidence.
next_experiment: None as written. Reconsider only a Proposal 4 mutation that first freezes a deterministic polynomial-time, basis-invariant binary fold computed from H and t without short-word enumeration, uses position-separated labels, proves polynomial rank, and states an analytic every-mixed-word invariant; then exactly test worst YES, best NO, kernels, affine closure, all-eight, holonomy, and exact-transfer rank.
